subject.title: feat: replace legacy exec approvals with V2

question: Should existing Windows nodes retain their legacy `exec-policy.json` behavior until an operator explicitly migrates, or is breaking those configured approvals acceptable for this release?
rationale: The policy formats authorize different things, full command text versus resolved executable paths, so code review cannot safely choose a migration semantic or an intentional breaking security boundary without maintainer direction.

options.title: Stage an explicit migration
options.body: Keep legacy policy behavior for existing installations until a backed-up, operator-visible V2 conversion is completed, with upgrade tests for allowed and denied commands.

options.title: Accept the breaking policy reset
options.body: Ship default-deny for every old policy, but document it as an intentional breaking change and provide an in-product recovery path for affected operators.

recommendation.title: Stage an explicit migration
recommendation.body: Keep legacy policy behavior for existing installations until a backed-up, operator-visible V2 conversion is completed, with upgrade tests for allowed and denied commands.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged V2 approval-dialog baseline whose persistence and authorization contract this PR extends.
